sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Lewis County, WA?
sections.html:
In Lewis County the Treasurer bills and collects, and the Assessor sets the value. The Treasurer's office is in the Historic Courthouse at 351 NW North Street in Chehalis, with a mailing address of PO Box 509, Chehalis, WA 98532. The Treasurer's number is 360-740-1115, and the Assessor's Office answers valuation questions at 360-740-1392.

The county's property tax page explains that a bill rests on three things: the taxable value from the Assessor, any special-use exemption that lowers that value, and the levy rate each taxing district adopts under state law. If a mortgage company pays your taxes you will not get a bill, so call the office if you expect a statement and nothing has come by mid-March.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Lewis County for a home seller?
sections.html:
Lewis County is a large, mostly rural county in Southwest Washington built along the Interstate 5 corridor. Chehalis is the county seat and Centralia is the largest city. The county covers about 2,403 square miles of land and touches eight other counties, and the Cascade Mountains and the Chehalis, Cowlitz and Nisqually river systems are part of its geography.

Other incorporated places include Morton, Mossyrock, Napavine, Toledo, Vader and Winlock, plus the town of Pe Ell. Lewis County was created in December 1845 by the Provisional Government of Oregon and named for Meriwether Lewis.

The Census Bureau's QuickFacts show how the market looks on paper:

  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 88,062, up 7.2% since April 2020.
  • Density: 34.2 people per square mile.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020-2024: $385,800.
  • Owner-occupied rate: 75.8%, with a median gross rent of $1,097.
  • Median household income: $74,796.
  • Building permits in 2025: 431.

sections.h2: When are Lewis County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Lewis County property taxes are due in two halves, April 30 and October 31, and any parcel with a bill of $50 or less is due in full on April 30. In 2026 the Treasurer set the second-half date at Monday, November 2, because October 31 fell on a Saturday. That date has now passed, so a balance left on a parcel you plan to sell is delinquent.

The statement for 2026 was scheduled to go out around February 13. The county offers e-statements and ACH payment, which draws the tax from a checking or savings account on the due date. A payment returned by the bank voids the payment and brings a $35 fee on top of any interest and penalty. Mail payments to the Lewis County Treasurer, PO Box 509, Chehalis, WA 98532, and mail them early, since the county measures timeliness by postmark.

sections.h2: What happens if I pay late in Lewis County?
sections.html:
Interest starts the first of the next month and is charged monthly on the unpaid tax. Residential property with four or fewer units, including mobile homes, pays 0.75% per month with no penalty. Nonresidential property and residential property with more than four units pays 1% per month, a one-time 3% penalty if still unpaid on June 1, and another one-time 8% if unpaid on December 1.

The Treasurer's FAQ adds a practical point: if you miss April 30, you can pay any time before October 31 and stop further charges by paying the first half plus whatever interest and penalty has accrued.

State law adds protection for some owners. Under RCW 84.56.020, the treasurer can offer payment agreements for past due taxes, and owners who meet the senior income test and live in the home can have interest and penalties waived shortly before the three-year mark if the parcel is already in a foreclosure action. The Treasurer must also send delinquent owners the contact number for the statewide foreclosure hotline.

sections.h2: How do I appeal my Lewis County property value?
sections.html:
Send a petition to the Lewis County Board of Equalization within 30 days of the date on your value change notice, or by July 1 of the assessment year, whichever is later. The county uses the 30-day window that RCW 84.40.038 sets as the default. The petition must have a copy of the notice attached or the Board treats it as incomplete.

The 2026 notices described values as of January 1, 2026 for taxes payable in 2027, built on 2025 sales. They are not tax bills. You can file three ways:

  • Online, through the form on the Board's page, with a scan or photo of the notice.
  • By mail to the Board of Equalization, 351 NW North St., Room 210, Chehalis, WA 98532.
  • In person at the Commissioners' Office, Room 210, on the second floor of the Historic Courthouse.

File a separate petition for each parcel and answer the four required questions: owner details, the land and improvement values you claim, your specific reasons, and power of attorney if someone files for you. The Board mails a hearing notice at least 30 days ahead. Hearings are held on Thursdays and Fridays, and evidence must arrive at least 21 business days before yours. The decision follows within 45 days, and a further appeal to the State Board of Tax Appeals is due within 30 days of the postmark.

The county's guide is blunt about what counts. The question is market value, and comparable sales from 2025 in your area carry the most weight. A neighbor's value, a percentage increase, hardship or the size of your bill do not establish market value. The Assessor's valuation is presumed correct, so you need clear, cogent and convincing evidence. Staff encourage a call to the Assessor first, because an agreement can let you withdraw the petition.

sections.h2: What counts as land and improvements on a Lewis County valuation notice?
sections.html:
The Assessor values land and improvements separately, and in Lewis County the word improvements covers more than the house. It includes garages, barns and outbuildings, wells, septic systems, utilities and driveways. Land is valued as if it were bare, so trees, vegetation and landscaping are left out of the land value.

That split is worth reading closely before a sale. If a well or septic system is failing or an outbuilding is gone, say so in a petition with photos or a repair estimate, because the petition asks for land and improvement values separately. The county also publishes 2025 sales data that you can filter by area to build a comparison.

sections.h2: Which relief programs can Lewis County owners use?
sections.html:
The senior and disabled persons exemption is the main program, and the Assessor's Office at 360-740-1392 administers it. Lewis County states that once the exemption is granted it does not need to be repaid. Under RCW 84.36.381, you qualify at 61 or older, when retired because of a disability, or as a veteran with the required VA rating, and you must own and live in the home. A surviving spouse or domestic partner can qualify from age 57 if the other spouse was receiving the exemption.

For owners in the lowest income tier, the statute fixes the valuation used for the exemption at the level in the year you first qualify, and it lets you transfer the exemption to a replacement home after a sale. Income limits and exempt amounts change for taxes payable in 2027, so ask the Assessor for the figures that apply to you. An owner turned down for the exemption can petition the Board of Equalization, using the form on the Board's forms page.

sections.h2: What should I expect at a Lewis County sale closing?
sections.html:
The Treasurer processes the real estate excise tax affidavit for deeded transfers. Lewis County asks for four printed copies of the affidavit, charges a $10 minimum to process one, and does not process transfers after 4 p.m., which gives the Auditor time to record before closing.

The state portion is graduated. For sales on or after January 1, 2027, the Department of Revenue lists 1.1% up to $551,000, 1.28% from there to $1,551,000, 2.75% to $3,051,000 and 3.0% above that. A local rate is added, and the county's REET page links the current local rates. The seller normally pays, and unpaid REET can become a lien on the property. Ask your escrow officer to request a tax payoff figure from the Treasurer before the closing date.

faqs.q: Who do I contact about property tax in Lewis County?
faqs.a: Call the Treasurer at 360-740-1115 for bills, payments and due dates, and the Assessor at 360-740-1392 for values and exemptions. The Board of Equalization takes appeals at 360-740-1391.

faqs.q: What interest does Lewis County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: A home with four or fewer units pays 0.75% interest per month and no penalty. Other property pays 1% per month plus a 3% penalty on June 1 and an 8% penalty on December 1.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Lewis County property value online?
faqs.a: Yes. The Board of Equalization takes petitions through an online form, by mail, or in person at Room 210 of the Historic Courthouse. Attach a copy of your value change notice, and file one petition per parcel.

faqs.q: Do I need to repay a Lewis County senior exemption?
faqs.a: No. The county says the exemption does not need to be repaid once it is granted. A tax deferral is different, so ask the Assessor which program you hold before you sell.

faqs.q: Does the Lewis County Treasurer process deeds on closing day?
faqs.a: Yes, but not after 4 p.m. Bring the excise tax affidavit copies early, and have your escrow officer confirm any tax payoff with the Treasurer ahead of time.
